entries.title: Save a page yourself when a site refuses
entries.body: Some sites turn Spideryarn away but let your own browser in. When adding an article fails and an upload is suggested, there is, on a computer, a Save for Spideryarn button to drag to your bookmarks bar: click it on the publisher's page to download the page, then upload the file. It removes the page's code and most of what was typed into forms, but visible personal details and text in editors can remain; Help explains. Robot-check pages at IEEE, Springer and JSTOR are recognised too, so they offer the upload instead of a message suggesting the address was wrong.

entries.title: Skim routes can stop at figures and tables
entries.body: Skim's route through an article can include its figures and tables, not just quotes. Each figure follows a quote in that quote's pass, at most one in Gist, two in More and three in Most, and shows its caption with, where there is one, a line saying why it is there; choosing it takes you to the whole figure. Routes planned before this need planning again to gain figures, and visitors to an article you have shared still see quotes only.

entries.title: Chat can bring a web page in
entries.body: When a Chat answer lists pages under From the web, or you paste a web address into your message, a Bring into this chat button adds that page to your library and attaches it to the chat, so you can ask about it alongside the article. This is in typed Chat.

entries.title: Sliders move only between settings that change something
entries.body: The sliders that set how much to show in Glossary, FAQ, Search, Quotes and the Citations list in Sources jump between the points where the list actually changes, with faint ticks marking each one. Before, most of a drag moved a number and nothing else. The arrow, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End keys step through the same points.

entries.title: Hints appear in the app's own cards
entries.body: The short explanations you see when pointing at a button or control appear in the app's own card across the reader, your library and the other pages, instead of the browser's plain tooltip. They also appear when you reach a control with the keyboard. On touch screens, tapping an open reading-time line again closes its card rather than reopening it.

entries.title: The guide can save a lightly reworded sentence
entries.body: In Chat's guide conversation, when you say why you are reading a piece or something about yourself, the guide can save that sentence with small tidying, like a capital letter, without asking. It says it was lightly reworded, shows the sentence it came from, and offers Undo. It adds to your About you text rather than replacing it.

entries.title: Untitled papers get the title printed on them
entries.body: Some papers that set their title page by hand were added under a made-up title from their first numbered part. The AI now picks the title out of the paper's opening, accepting only words printed there, and otherwise uses the paper's arXiv number or address. Link previews and Chat's reading of web pages no longer use the made-up title either.

entries.title: Following a link keeps the passage in view
entries.body: Following a link to a particular figure or passage deep in a long section could leave it well below the window once the page finished laying out, for example when the controls bar appeared. It stays centred where you arrived.
